observation_summary: The application throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when attempting to find a wrap position in a string that contains no whitespace characters, because the code attempts to access a character at an index equal to the string length.
hypothesis: The while loop condition in findWrapPos incorrectly uses 'pos <= text.length()' as a guard, allowing the code to attempt to access 'text.charAt(text.length())', which is out of bounds. The logic intended to scan for whitespace characters beyond the wrap point is flawed and unnecessary for the intended behavior of simply chopping at the width.
prediction: Removing the while loop that performs the out-of-bounds character access will resolve the exception and correctly return the wrap position at the specified width.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the removal of the entire while loop that contained the problematic 'pos <= text.length()' condition and the 'text.charAt(pos)' call. This confirms that the loop was the source of the out-of-bounds error and that the logic was redundant or incorrect for the desired behavior.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic boundary condition error where a loop condition allowed an index to reach the length of the string, causing an out-of-bounds access. The fix involved removing the incorrect validation/loop logic entirely. This falls squarely under 'Checking' as it pertains to incorrect predicate logic and boundary validation.
evidence_used: The stack trace shows java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at HelpFormatter.java:937
The buggy code at line 937 uses 'pos <= text.length()' in a while loop condition
The fix diff removes the entire while loop that performed the out-of-bounds access

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the loop is part of the method's logic, the root cause is specifically the incorrect boundary check in the loop condition that leads to an out-of-bounds exception, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
